item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-7a0634dc4f666d08","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"On 10 March 2023, President Félix Tshisekedi told a visiting UN Security Council delegation that the DRC was an attacked country and characterized Rwanda's support for the M23 as aggression and a violation of international law, asking the Council to assume responsibility; the delegation said it supported the DRC and condemned violations of Congolese sovereignty.","question_ids":["2B.3","2B.6","2B.9","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; the source is a presidential account of the meeting and includes the delegation's stated response.","ruler_attribution":"Direct presidential statement and meeting action; the characterization of Rwanda and M23 is presented by the DRC presidency.","limitations":["The source does not independently verify the factual or legal characterization of the conflict.","No concrete ceasefire, settlement, or corrective action is documented in this unit."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7a7929777266dd94","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The World Bank reported that the DRC authorities had implemented an ambitious economic-governance reform program despite difficult conditions, including treasury and accounting reforms, stronger public procurement procedures, digitization of domestic revenue mobilization, implementation of the 2020 Telecom Law, competitive appointments for power and water utilities and the national road fund, strengthened oversight of the Mining Fund for Future Generations, procedures for transferring state-owned mining assets, and milestones toward reviewing forest concessions.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","8B.2","8B.4","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The operation was approved on 29 March 2023 and describes reforms implemented or supported by that date; attribution to the ruler is indirect through the Congolese authorities.","ruler_attribution":"The World Bank attributes the program to the Congolese authorities and describes it as the government's reform program; it does not isolate Tshisekedi's personal decisions.","limitations":["The source reports reform measures and institutional actions, but not their full execution quality or outcomes.","External World Bank financing and support are material contributors."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7a7929777266dd94","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"On 29 March 2023, the World Bank approved a $500 million development-policy operation supporting DRC economic-governance reforms and a $400 million project for girls' learning and empowerment, focused on secondary-school quality and access, keeping adolescent girls in school, safer and more inclusive schools, and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Approval occurred within 2023; the projects are planned or supported interventions rather than completed outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"The projects support the Congolese government's reform and education objectives, but the source does not establish that Tshisekedi personally designed or funded them.","limitations":["The source documents financing and intended mechanisms, not realized welfare outcomes.","IDA financing and World Bank implementation support limit attribution to the ruler."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7a7929777266dd94","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The World Bank reported that DRC's free-primary-education policy, implemented since 2019, was associated with more than 3.6 million additional students enrolled in public primary schools in 2021–2022 compared with 2017–2018.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The comparison includes 2021–2022, within the target ruler-period context, but the policy began before 2023 and the result is not a 2023-only measure.","ruler_attribution":"The World Bank attributes the policy to the Congolese government; the source does not establish Tshisekedi's exclusive causal responsibility.","limitations":["The enrollment increase is not proof of learning quality, affordability, completion, or equitable access.","The result predates the 2023 target year and may reflect multiple actors and factors."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7709c16b1e36ae58","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"In its 2023 decision on DRC World Heritage properties, UNESCO regretted that the State Party had not submitted the implementation report requested in 2021 and noted alleged human-rights abuses against Indigenous peoples and local communities during law-enforcement operations; it requested a national eco-guard code of conduct, a grievance mechanism, human-rights training, and rights-based participation of affected communities.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.7","5B.7","6B.8","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"UNESCO adopted the decision in 2023; the findings concern the State Party and operations associated with protected-area governance.","ruler_attribution":"Institutional finding about the DRC State Party; the source does not attribute the alleged abuses or reporting failure personally to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The decision reports allegations and institutional non-compliance, not a final judicial determination against the ruler.","It does not specify which officials or agencies were responsible."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7709c16b1e36ae58","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"UNESCO reported improved security in Salonga, Kahuzi-Biega, and Garamba National Parks, but continued security challenges in Okapi Wildlife Reserve and severe conflict in Virunga National Park, where rebel control and fighting since 2022 had again resulted in park staff being killed; it urged the State Party to strengthen ICCN capacity and restore peace and security.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","8B.5","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The decision is from 2023 and assesses conditions existing during the reporting period; some conflict began in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"UNESCO addresses the DRC State Party and ICCN, not Tshisekedi personally; external rebel activity is a major constraint.","limitations":["The source documents security conditions and recommendations, not the ruler's specific orders, resources, or implementation response.","The mixed finding spans multiple parks and cannot be generalized to all domestic security."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7709c16b1e36ae58","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"UNESCO strongly regretted that the DRC's 2022 public auction included two oil blocks overlapping Virunga National Park, expressed concern about semi-industrial mining in Okapi Wildlife Reserve, reiterated that mining and oil activities are incompatible with World Heritage status, and urged cancellation of overlapping concessions; it requested a detailed implementation report by 1 February 2024.","question_ids":["5B.4","5B.5","5B.7","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The UNESCO decision was adopted in 2023 and evaluates the State Party's 2022 auction and ongoing activities.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns the DRC State Party and its concession decisions; personal responsibility of Tshisekedi is not established.","limitations":["The source does not state whether the requested cancellations were later implemented.","The decision reflects UNESCO's conservation mandate and does not assess all economic consequences."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-38b387a4b6d47e10","SRC-a8869733d814c822","SRC-aaedf11b987deb19","SRC-493f137a50b17b72","SRC-cdb288db3b1e4214","SRC-9647d7fea6fcd53e","SRC-8d665d40104d0386","SRC-1e6278fdb2f494d4","SRC-bafd0a259785395f"],"batch_limitations":["Several supplied documents contain only page navigation, metadata, abstracts, or paywalled content and provide no concrete 2023 fact.","The 2024 UNESCO Okapi decision was excluded from the facts because the target period is 2023, although it may document later follow-up on 2023-era conservation issues.","No supplied source provides material evidence for nuclear-risk questions 1B.1-1B.10."]}
